parsed.draft: Hi Aman, looking forward to both calls on the fifth. Attached is our API pricing sheet, ahead of the pricing call. Arjun

next_move.what: Send Aman our API pricing sheet before the pricing call on the fifth of October.

facts.claim: Aman Verma, founder of Memloop, set two calls for the fifth of October — product in the morning, pricing in the afternoon IST — and asked for our API pricing sheet before the second.
facts.quote: API pricing sheet before the second one? Aman Verma Founder, Memloop

facts.claim: Both calls are booked for the fifth of October.
His ask is open and waits on us.
The engine reads the file both as account administration and as a sales opportunity.

inferences.claim: The pricing call is built around the sheet: without it in hand beforehand, the call cannot do what Aman set it up to do.
Memloop asking for our API pricing suggests they are weighing paid use of our API, not only a design partnership.

patterns.claim: The file is new — seen once in each domain, with no earlier card or outcome — so there is no record of Memloop's pace.

hypotheses.proposition: The pricing sheet may not yet exist in a form we would send.
hypotheses.needs: Arjun's word on whether a current API pricing sheet is ready.

hypotheses.proposition: Aman may expect pricing shaped for a design partner.
hypotheses.needs: The product call, or a question to him.

unknowns.question: Is our API pricing settled enough to put in writing?
unknowns.relevance: If not, it must be settled before the second call, and the sheet may carry ranges rather than prices.

unknowns.question: Who from our side should join each call?
unknowns.relevance: The product call may need an engineer; the pricing call needs whoever owns pricing.

unknowns.question: Did the sheet reach Aman by another channel?
unknowns.relevance: If so, the ask is closed and only the calls remain.

frames.primary: A design partner moving fast: two calls on one day, and the pricing sheet he asked for is ours to send before the second.
rivals: A buyer pricing our API, where the sheet opens a negotiation rather than answering a courtesy.
A busy partner who will be content to see pricing on screen during the call.

expected_vs_actual.expected: From Aman's own words and the brief's goal of landing design partners: the API pricing sheet with Aman before the pricing call on the fifth.
expected_vs_actual.actual: Nothing from us is in the file; the ask is open and both calls are booked.

scenarios.do_nothing: The pricing call opens without the sheet Aman asked for, and its time goes on what he wanted to have read beforehand.
scenarios.act: Sending the sheet before the fifth lets Aman bring questions to the pricing call and move toward terms.
scenarios.best: The sheet goes out early, both calls go well, and Memloop moves to a design-partner agreement with pricing settled.
scenarios.worst: No sheet, a wasted pricing call, and a partner who reads the gap as unreadiness.
signals_to_watch: The pricing sheet sent to Aman before the second call
Aman writing again before the fifth

reasons: Landing design partners is a goal the brief names, and Memloop is one of the brief's design partner talks.
Aman asked for the sheet before a call booked on a fixed date.
A late sheet can still be sent, so a slip costs a weaker call, not the partner.

parsed.alternative: If the pricing is not ready to put in writing, tell Aman before the fifth what the sheet will cover, and walk him through it in the pricing call.
parsed.wait_or_stop: No waiting — the ask is ours; once the sheet is sent, the file waits for the calls on the fifth.
parsed.done_when: Aman has our API pricing sheet before the pricing call.
